page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Set up 2ⁿ = 512
steps.margin_note: First mark. Name the unknown, then write |P(A)| = 2ⁿ. The equation 2ⁿ = 512 is the line being marked, even if the arithmetic afterwards slips.
lines: Let n be the number of elements in A.
A set with n elements has 2ⁿ subsets, so |P(A)| = 2ⁿ

recall.must_convey: That |P(A)| = 2ⁿ, so the equation to solve is 2ⁿ = 512.
accept: the power set has two power n elements so two power n equals five hundred twelve
let n be the number of elements and use two to the n
write two power n equals five twelve
two power n equals five hundred twelve ani rayali
set up the equation with two to the power n

steps.why: The whole question is one rule used backwards. Writing 2ⁿ = 512 turns a set question into an index equation, which is the only step where the set theory is used.
steps.memory_tip: The count is always 2 raised to the number of elements, never the number of elements raised to 2.
common_mistakes: Reading 512 as the number of elements in A rather than in P(A).

steps.label: Write 512 as a power of 2
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Show 512 as 2⁹ rather than stating it. Once the bases match, the powers can be equated and n is read off.
lines: The bases are equal, so the powers are equal, and n = 9.

accept: five hundred twelve is two to the ninth so n is nine
keep halving five twelve until you reach one and count nine steps
match the powers of two and get nine
five hundred twelve ante two power nine so n nine

steps.why: Two powers of the same base are equal only when the powers are equal, so writing 512 as 2⁹ is what allows n to be read off. Halving 512 nine times down to 1 is the same check done by counting.
steps.memory_tip: Powers of 2 worth knowing by heart: 2⁶ = 64, 2⁷ = 128, 2⁸ = 256, 2⁹ = 512, 2¹⁰ = 1024.
common_mistakes: Answering 512 or 256, which are counts of subsets, not of elements.
Dividing 512 by 2 once and giving 256 as n.
Writing 512 = 2⁸ by counting the halvings one short.
